question: How can Shiva be known if he is not directly perceived by the mind?
premises: A tree can be known from its visible form even when taste and other qualities are not directly perceived.
Conceptual thought can infer an object from partial indicators.
Sound, point, and related signs can serve as indicators of Shiva.
inference: Shiva can be known through indicative signs such as sound and point, even though he is not directly grasped by ordinary mental perception.
uncertainties: The technical scope of nāda-bindu-ādi is compressed in this verse.
plain_english: Just as one can recognize a tree from its form even without directly perceiving its taste and other qualities, so too one can know Shiva through signs such as sound and point.
